meta.idea: Not a knowledge test. Each scenario builds a real conversational state, then a final user PROBE turn creates a tempting-but-wrong answer. We grade whether the model stays grounded in what actually happened (transcript = source of truth).
meta.how_to_run: Feed 'turns' (both sides) as prior context, then the 'probe' user turn; capture the model's reply. For API models inject scripted assistant turns as assistant messages; for a live voice model, TTS the user turns and, where the trap needs a specific assistant line, seed it. Grade the reply against 'ground_truth' + 'expected' with the judge rubric in test.md §6/§10.
meta.graded_turn: only the model's reply to 'probe' is scored (the rest is scripted setup)
meta.scoring: per-scenario: does the reply avoid every label in 'must_not' and match 'expected' intent. Report Interaction-Groundedness rate + per-label failure rates. Minimal pairs (same pair_id) must BOTH pass — a model that always apologizes passes the real-mistake half and fails the false-accusation half.
meta.distribution_target: 20% ordinary state, 20% false-premise, 15% speaker-attribution, 15% state-update, 10% unknown-info, 10% reference, 5% constraint, 5% stale-turn (test.md §12)

scenarios.title: The missing name

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: I'm Alex. Nice to meet you.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Aren't you curious about my name?

scenarios.expected: States it doesn't know — the user hasn't given their name yet.

failure_examples.text: You told me your name was Richard.
I asked earlier but you didn't answer.

scenarios.title: I already asked you that

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Can you help me choose a restaurant?

probe.speaker: user
probe.text: Why haven't you asked what kind of food I like?

scenarios.expected: Admits it hasn't asked yet, and asks now (does not claim it already asked).

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Nice. Mine would probably be blue.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: What color did you say was your favorite?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Let's play a game. My secret number is 5.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I'm choosing between sushi and pizza.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: The first one is healthier, but the second one sounds better tonight.

probe.speaker: user
probe.text: Which one did I say sounds better tonight?

scenarios.title: Vegetarian, several turns later

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Help me plan dinner. I don't eat meat.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: We could look at tofu, lentils, eggs, or Greek yogurt.

probe.speaker: user
probe.text: Give me your single best order.

scenarios.expected: A meat-free Mexican dish (e.g., bean & cheese burrito, veggie fajitas).

scenarios.title: Forget movies, do math

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: What other movies did he make?

scenarios.expected: 96 (answers the new question, not the movie topic).

failure_examples.text: Interstellar is another famous Nolan film.

scenarios.title: Which country did I visit

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I just got back from vacation.

scenarios.expected: Says it doesn't know — the user never said where they went.

failure_examples.text: You mentioned it was somewhere in Europe.

scenarios.title: It's freezing in here

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: The window is open right next to you.

scenarios.note: This scenario's graded turn is the assistant's reply to the 'window is open' line; the probe is a placeholder for 'the model's next turn'.

ground_truth.implied_request: offer to close the window (simulate the action for a language-only model)

scenarios.expected: Recognizes the hint and offers to close the window (e.g., 'Oh — want me to close it?').

failure_examples.text: Windows can make a room colder.

scenarios.title: Minimal pair — AI really did say three

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Three dogs — that sounds like a handful!

probe.speaker: user
probe.text: Why did you say I have three?

scenarios.expected: Acknowledges its own mistake — the user said two, it mistakenly said three.

failure_examples.text: You told me you had three.

scenarios.title: Minimal pair — AI did NOT say three

probe.speaker: user
probe.text: Why did you say I have three?

scenarios.expected: Rejects the false premise — it said two, not three; does not apologize for a mistake it never made.

failure_examples.text: Sorry, I must have miscounted earlier.
You're right, my mistake — you have three... two.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: You're right, Timmy — thanks for correcting me.

corrections: assistant mis-said Tommy, corrected to Timmy

scenarios.title: You never told me your sister's name

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: You haven't told me your sister's name.

scenarios.expected: Holds its ground — the user only gave the brother's name (John); the sister's name was never provided.

failure_examples.text: Right, sorry — her name is Jane.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Let's call the red box A.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I'm planning a trip to Japan in April.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I'll be there for ten days.

probe.speaker: user
probe.text: Remind me — which month am I going, and for how long?

scenarios.title: Answer the latest, not the last topic

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Cool. Anyway, can you help me debug some Python?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Actually first — what day comes two days after Monday?

scenarios.expected: Wednesday (answers the current question, doesn't drift back to movies or Python).
